gourmet.hero_title:
Take your time exploring
the flavors of Yamagata.
gourmet.description: Regional dishes, noodles, fruit and cafés: a fictional guide to Yamagata flavors.
gourmet.subtitle: Stories about the tastes of Yamagata
gourmet.about: This is a fictional food guide. Articles are demonstrations, not reviews or verified business information.

gourmet:imoni-guide.title: Autumn means imoni gatherings
gourmet:imoni-guide.summary: A seasonal story about the famous Yamagata riverside imoni parties.
gourmet:imoni-guide.cover_alt: A photorealistic demo image of a pot of Yamagata imoni
gourmet:imoni-guide.markdown:
In autumn, Yamagata comes alive with imoni gatherings. Friends and neighbors meet by the river to share a large pot of taro stew—an occasion that feels like a seasonal tradition.

Soy sauce or miso? Different ingredients and regional styles make the conversation as good as the food.

gourmet:yonezawa-ramen.title: Exploring Yonezawa ramen
gourmet:yonezawa-ramen.summary: Curly, fine noodles and clear broth in a comforting local bowl.
gourmet:yonezawa-ramen.cover_alt: A photo-style image of a bowl of Yonezawa ramen
gourmet:yonezawa-ramen.markdown:
A gentle soy sauce broth paired with delicate, curly noodles gives Yonezawa ramen its distinctive appeal. It is the kind of bowl you could happily return to again and again.

This sample introduces it as both a memorable meal on a trip and a familiar everyday taste.

gourmet:fruit-dessert.title: A sweet moment with Yamagata fruit
gourmet:fruit-dessert.summary: A fictional food diary of fruit parfaits and desserts in Yamagata.
gourmet:fruit-dessert.cover_alt: A photo-style image of cherries growing on a tree
gourmet:fruit-dessert.markdown:
Cherries, grapes and La France pears are among Yamagata’s delights. Seasonal sweets appear in cafés and pastry shops across this fruit-growing region.

This sample article imagines simple desserts that let the fruit’s own flavor shine.

gourmet:onsen-cafe.title: A café break in an onsen town
gourmet:onsen-cafe.summary: A fictional café stop while strolling through a Yamagata hot-spring town.
gourmet:onsen-cafe.cover_alt: A photo-style image of a wooden café in the mountains
gourmet:onsen-cafe.markdown:
Beyond the rising steam is a small café. A coffee break during a stroll is a lovely way to experience the slower rhythm of a place.

This demo is written as a light, travel-diary-style food story.

gourmet:kirikiri-tendo.title: Tendo's Eatery "Kirikiri" — Tendon with Large Kakiage
gourmet:kirikiri-tendo.summary: A soba restaurant in Takadama, Tendo City, reopened as an eatery. Its kakiage tendon, braised pork belly, and homemade pudding are highly acclaimed.
gourmet:kirikiri-tendo.cover_alt: A watercolor-style illustration of a large kakiage tendon
gourmet:kirikiri-tendo.markdown:
The soba restaurant "Kirikiri" in Takadama, Tendo City, has reopened as an eatery.

According to a Threads post, the tendon topped with a large kakiage is crispy and filling. The melt-in-your-mouth braised pork belly (a la carte) and the brown sugar pudding (with homemade coffee caramel sauce) were also delicious. A place worth considering if you are undecided on where to have lunch in Tendo.

gourmet:satonishiki-imoni-lunch.title: Higashine "Sato Nishiki" Imoni Lunch — Imoni, Onigiri, and Homemade Side Dishes
gourmet:satonishiki-imoni-lunch.summary: An imoni lunch offered by Sato Nishiki in Higashine City. The set comes with imoni, onigiri, and homemade side dishes, and there are cherry sweets as well.
gourmet:satonishiki-imoni-lunch.cover_alt: Watercolor-style illustration of an imoni lunch
gourmet:satonishiki-imoni-lunch.markdown:
At "Sato Nishiki" in Higashine City, you can enjoy a lunch featuring Yamagata's famous imoni.

According to a post on Threads, the lunch is a set of imoni, onigiri, and homemade side dishes, and there are also sweets made with cherries. The post notes that imoni in the inland region is soy-sauce-based, with ingredients such as taro, beef, konjac, burdock root, mushrooms, and green onions, and that autumn "imoni gatherings" are a seasonal tradition in Yamagata.

gourmet:okuyama-shokudo-murayama.title: Murayama "Okuyama Shokudo" — Kamado-Cooked Rice and a Big Fried Shrimp
gourmet:okuyama-shokudo-murayama.summary: A diner in Murayama City, Yamagata Prefecture. Rice cooked in an old-fashioned kamado, a big fried shrimp, and a motsu nikomi set meal are introduced.
gourmet:okuyama-shokudo-murayama.cover_alt: Watercolor-style illustration of a fried shrimp set meal
gourmet:okuyama-shokudo-murayama.markdown:
"Okuyama Shokudo" in Murayama City, Yamagata Prefecture, is a diner reputed for its kamado-cooked rice and handmade dishes.

According to an Instagram post (@odekake.spot.tohoku), the owner trained at Michelin-listed restaurants and overseas, and started the shop wanting local people to eat good rice. Recommended dishes include a big fried shrimp with homemade tartar sauce, and a gently flavored motsu nikomi set meal. With tatami, counter, and table seating, it is introduced as a place easy to use alone or with family.
